name: Shanghai Biennale
funding: Run by the state-owned Power Station of Art; budget undisclosed and paid mainly from Shanghai city government funds. 2025 partners: Aesop, Denza, Langham hotels and lighting maker Flos.

name: TANK Shanghai
funding: Founded by collector and karaoke-club owner Qiao Zhibing, who told The Art Newspaper he paid for it. The government-backed West Bund Group invited him and manages the surrounding park.

name: West Bund Museum
funding: Run and paid for by the state-owned West Bund Group. The Centre Pompidou partnership was renewed in 2023 for five years. Joint shows since 2019 drew over 2 million visitors.

name: Yuz Museum
funding: In 2019 Qatar Museums joined LACMA and Yuz in a partnership. LACMA said its role is support for exhibition programming. Hyundai presented the first show.

name: OCAT Shenzhen
funding: Founded 2005 and owned by OCT Group, a central state-owned tourism and property group. OCT cut funding sharply in 2023 to venue costs only; OCAT must earn its own income.

name: Hubei Museum of Art
funding: Provincial public museum under the Hubei Dept of Culture and Tourism, funded through the provincial budget (2026 unit budget filed).

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Yinchuan
funding: Founded 2012-15 by Ningxia Minsheng Real Estate (property developer) with the provincial government under a BOT deal; about 300m yuan build.

name: Fragmentos, Espacio de Arte y Memoria
funding: Colombian Ministry of Culture space run by the Museo Nacional.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá
Lugar a Dudas
funding: Non-profit cultural foundation supported by Prince Claus Fund, DOEN Foundation, artist philanthropy from Oscar Muñoz, and international grants.

name: Museo La Tertulia
funding: Private museum, ~2,000 works (2025); funded by Colegio Alemán de Cali as major patron, Bancolombia, Fundación Sura, Comfandi and Fundación Scarpetta Gnecco.

name: Casa Tres Patios (C3P)
funding: Its financial information page lists restricted donations from Foundation For Arts Iniciative, Fundación Sofía Pérez de Soto, Fundación SURA and Arts Collaboratory.
